sources.finding: Pixel is a two-component integer field. The Image domain controls the coordinates; this is not a constant vector.
Native Pixel coordinates add the domain data offset to each texel. This first port qualifies only full-frame zero-offset domains. Uniform and Normalized use distinct float2 math and are excluded.

Native CPU int2-to-float averages both components; int2-to-int uses math::midpoint, and Boolean tests whether either component is nonzero. The qualified Pixel coordinates are nonnegative <=8191, so half-sum and tie-toward-X midpoint are exactly representable.
Native GPU int2 scalar conversion delegates to float2 averaging; int conversion calls midpoint; Boolean tests that the pair is not all zero. These are separate from float3 averaging.
